title: Unified Inference Q2 2026: PRD, Design Specs, Roadmap & Pricing Notes + Release Notes
author: Sofia Martinez
content:
Overview
--------
This document consolidates the product overview, PRD (requirements), high-level design specs, roadmap and themes, pricing & packaging notes, and release notes for Unified Inference (U-Inf) work delivered in Q2 2026. It is intended for product, engineering, solutions, and GTM stakeholders.

Objectives
----------
- Provide a single reference for cross-functional teams evaluating or operating the Unified Inference product.
- Capture acceptance criteria and non-functional requirements used for release gating.
- Summarize roadmap priorities and pricing changes that impact customers and partners.

1) Product overview (summary)
--------------------------------
Unified Inference provides a single API and operational model across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The Q2 2026 release focuses on:
- Model routing and cost-aware fallbacks (improved policy primitives).
- Runtime improvements to reduce p99 generation latency by 12–18% for multi-turn chat workloads.
- Pricing/packaging updates to introduce per-request tiering for batch embeddings and reserved throughput credits for Dedicated customers.

Why this matters
- Customers get predictable latency and lower unit costs through smarter routing and caching.
- Platform teams can standardize on one API while choosing the right cost/performance tradeoff per route.

2) PRD: Goals and high-level requirements
------------------------------------------
Goals (prioritized)
1. Improve tail latency for multi-turn chat to meet SLO (p99 <= 550ms for short prompts on dedicated NVLink pools).
2. Introduce model-routing primitives that allow policy-based fallback to lower-cost model families under capacity constraints.
3. Offer a straightforward pricing option for large embedding batches and a reserved throughput credit for Dedicated customers.
4. Maintain backwards compatibility for core text-generation and chat endpoints.

Success metrics (target values)
- Latency: p50 <= 70ms, p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 550ms (short prompts, dedicated baseline).
- Cost: 10–25% reduction in average cost-per-token for workloads benefiting from routing + caching.
- Reliability: >= 99.95% availability for Dedicated routes (monthly).
- Adoption: 30% of active Dedicated customers adopt reserved throughput credits within 3 months of GA.

Functional requirements (table)
| id | requirement | acceptance criteria | owner | priority |
| R1 | Model routing policies (policy language) | Policies allow routing by latency budget, cost budget, region, and model capability tag; unit tests & e2e validation | eng-serving-runtime | high |
| R2 | Fallback model variants | Automatic fallback to verified model variants (e.g., fp16->int8 quant) when capacity constrained; no data leakage across private deployments | eng-platform | high |
| R3 | Reserved throughput credits | UI/API + billing integration for customers to purchase monthly throughput credits; meters consumed credits and exposes usage | finance-and-legal | medium |
| R4 | Embedding batch pricing option | Bulk embedding endpoint with commit-based pricing tiers and a 24-hour job window for queued batches | product | medium |
| R5 | Backwards compatibility | Existing client SDKs and API contracts remain valid; deprecation path for breaking changes must be documented | eng-developer-experience | high |

Non-functional requirements
- Security: All control-plane traffic for Private must be reachable only within customer VPCs; audit logs retained 365 days for enterprise customers.
- Observability: Per-route token-level cost and latency metrics shipped to Console; tracing must include selected kernel and quantization profile.
- Performance: Automatic prefix caching should not increase median latency by >5% for cached requests.

3) Design specs (high level)
----------------------------
A. Routing & policy engine
- New policy DSL (yaml/json) supports match conditions: route, user_tier, latency_budget_ms, cost_budget_usd_per_1k_tokens, region, model_tag.
- Policy evaluation is performed at the edge proxy; decisions are cached for 30s to avoid thundering herd.
- Fall back rules include soft fallback (best-effort) and hard fallback (guaranteed).

B. Runtime kernel selection & quantization profiles
- Runtime exposes a kernel selector API populated via the model catalog. Selection inputs: seq_len_estimate, kv_cache_hit_rate, quant_profile_id, target_latency_ms.
- Profiling data from the benchmarking suite (eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite) feeds automatic suggestions to a model's default quant_profile.

C. Billing & credits model
- Reserved throughput credits are represented as monthly time-windowed tokens with overridable burst limits.
- Billing events emitted to Kafka with schema: event_type, customer_id, route_id, tokens_charged, credit_consumed, timestamp. (Note: actual event metadata documented in billing-schemas page).

D. Console UX changes
- New UI panels: "Throughput Credits" and "Bulk Embeddings" settings under Billing.
- Per-route cost breakdown shows routing decisions and credit consumption.

4) Roadmap and themes (next 6 months)
-------------------------------------
Themes
- Production economics: tooling and defaults that reduce per-unit cost without sacrificing SLOs.
- Unified developer experience: same API semantics and rollout controls across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Enterprise readiness: stronger audit, retention, and network controls for Private deployments.

Planned milestones
- 2026-05: Policy DSL v1 (beta) + integration tests.
- 2026-06: Reserved throughput credits (alpha) + billing pipeline integration.
- 2026-07: Runtime p99 improvements deployed to Dedicated NVLink pools.
- 2026-08: Bulk embeddings pricing & queued-job window GA.
- 2026-09: Policy v1 GA + Console rollout and migrations docs.

Dependencies & risks
- Dependency: Billing pipeline updates (finance-and-legal + eng-infra) to support credit semantics.
- Risk: Kernel selector changes could regress tail latency if profiling signals are noisy. Mitigation: staged canary and automatic rollback.

5) Pricing and packaging notes (summary)
--------------------------------------
High-level changes
- Introduce "Reserved Throughput Credits" SKU for Dedicated customers: monthly commitment with a forecasted tokens/month and burst allowance.
- Bulk embedding tiers: per-batch queued window with stepped pricing (S1: up to 10M tokens/month, S2: 10–100M, S3: >100M).
- No price increases for existing per-token generation customers; routing optimizations may reduce their effective bill.

Billing examples (illustrative)
- Customer A (Dedicated) purchases 50M tokens/month credit. Their committed price = $X/month + 0.8 * standard per-token for burst usage beyond credit.
- Customer B (Hosted) moves 75% of embedding jobs to Bulk Embeddings and sees a 20% reduction in invoice line for embeddings.

Packaging recommendations
- Offer a bundled pilot: 3-month trial of Reserved Credits at 50% discount for customers migrating from BYO-infra.
- Add a Sales playbook entry detailing how to position credits for platform and cost-conscious engineering teams.

6) Release notes (Q2 2026 GA highlights)
----------------------------------------
Release highlights (2026-06-15)
- Model routing policy engine (beta): allows customers to declare latency and cost budgets per-route.
- Reserved throughput credits (alpha): early access for selected Dedicated customers with billing integration and Console visibility.
- Runtime performance: p99 improved by ~15% in NVLink-backed Dedicated clusters for multi-turn chat.
- Bulk Embeddings (beta): new endpoint with queued-job semantics and tiered pricing.

Bug fixes & smaller improvements
- Fixed an edge case where KV cache warm-up caused a transient increase in p95 for sequences >1024 tokens.
- Console: fixed incorrect credit usage display for multi-tenant accounts.
- SDK: node and python SDKs patched to include policy_v1 examples and new billing event hooks.

Known issues and next steps
- Known: Policy DSL v1 may incorrectly prioritize cost_budget over latency_budget in some multi-condition rules. A hotfix is scheduled for 2026-06-22.
- Next steps: expand Reserved Credits GA to additional Dedicated customers (target: +20 customers by 2026-07-15); complete policy DSL GA and full Console rollout by 2026-09.

Operational runbook (short)
--------------------------
If customers report increased tail latency after policy changes:
1. Validate policy decision via request trace (trace_id) in Console.
2. Check kernelselector and quant_profile in the trace; revert policy to previous stable if fallback triggered unexpectedly.
3. Escalate to eng-serving-runtime oncall and open a P0 if >5% customer impact is observed in the last 15min window.
